headline: Nobel laureate Maria Corina Machado returns from exile, defying the US-backed interim order
dek: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday Oct 25 after more than 10 months abroad/exile, announcing 'I am here. With you.' on X.
sources: Maria Corina Machado's own X post ('Estoy aqui. Con ustedes.'); Edmundo Gonzalez confirmation on X; Reuters witness at the Lara church
fault_line: Return as liberation vs return as destabilisation: does Machado's homecoming force the election Washington keeps postponing, or risk the reconciliation deal that freed prisoners and let exiles return?

sections.what_happened: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday Oct 25 after more than 10 months abroad/exile, announcing 'I am here. With you.' on X. She appeared at the Church of Santa Rosa in Barquisimeto (Lara state), greeted by supporters chanting 'liberty', and was travelling by road toward Caracas, per her team. Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia, who ran in her place in 2024 and is recognised by the US and others as that election's winner, confirmed her return and said he would join her 'very soon'. Entry route was initially undisclosed; Reuters sources later said she flew privately Panama to Colombia, then crossed overland. Trump, asked Sunday, said he knew nothing about it ('She's a very nice woman... we're doing really well in Venezuela'), restating backing for interim president Delcy Rodriguez; Secretary of State Rubio said her safe return was 'the direct result of the US supported reconciliation talks' that freed hundreds of political prisoners. Context: Maduro was removed by US forces in January 2026; Rodriguez, his former deputy, has stayed on as interim president past the initial 90-day mandate with no election scheduled, and Trump said in September it was too soon for elections.
sections.what_verified: Return confirmed by Machado herself, by Gonzalez, and by a Reuters witness at the church; the Panama-Colombia-overland route is an ATTRIBUTED REPORT from two sources cited by Reuters, not a confirmed itinerary.
sections.what_disputed: The political effect is unresolved: Rodriguez remains interim president with US backing and no election date; Rubio's framing (return as a product of US-backed talks) contests the opposition's framing (return as a challenge to the interim order). Machado's own team did not disclose how she entered, and the overland route rests on unnamed sources. USA Today also carried the return but has NO declared tier in the registry and is NOT counted.
sections.why_matters: The Nobel laureate Washington sidelined just walked back in -- while the interim president it backs stays put, past her mandate, with no election date.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Sunday Oct 25, in no prior scan) -- Venezuela: Nobel laureate Maria Corina Machado returns from exile, defying the US-backed interim order

totw_analysis: Our read: The Nobel laureate Washington sidelined just walked back in -- while the interim president it backs stays put, past her mandate, with no election date. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Return as liberation vs return as destabilisation: does Machado's homecoming force the election Washington keeps postponing, or risk the reconciliation deal that freed prisoners and let exiles return?
